subject: Post-call recap: cost & capacity tradeoffs for StratusPay (pilot scope & next steps)
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@stratuspay.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: cost & capacity tradeoffs for StratusPay (pilot scope & next steps)

Hi Alicia — thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we stay aligned.

Key pain points you shared:
- Current conversational payments flows are driving unpredictable token spend (spikes on peak settlement windows).
- Budget constraint: leadership gave a tight inference budget target (~$250k/year) for model-driven features.
- Latency SLO: 200–300ms p95 for critical payment flows; some non-critical flows can tolerate higher latency.
- Need to preserve output quality for authorization prompts (false positives have business impact).

What we discussed (summary):
- Baseline: you run an ensemble of an Llama-2 style model for chat + smaller embedding calls for similarity; combined average token/interaction today ~1.6k tokens.
- Levers we recommended: batching (short window tail to consolidate concurrent requests), prefix/KV caching for repeated authorization prompts, and a quantized runtime for lower-cost model variants.
- Pilot ask: 3-week technical pilot (integration + ops validation) with a focus on token-economics and SLO validation.

Preliminary TCO framing (attached: stratuspay-tco-v1.xlsx):
- Baseline spend (your reported numbers): ~450M tokens/month -> estimated $X/month (sheet shows calculations).
- Conservative pilot estimate (with batching + prefix caching + int8 quantized model): unit cost reduction range 35–55% depending on traffic shape and cache hit-rate.
- Important sensitivity: small increases in concurrency (bursting) are where batching yields the biggest marginal savings.

Risks and constraints:
- If authorization prompts are highly variable (low reuse), prefix caching lift will be limited.
- Some model variants may require evaluation for quality regressions post-quantization — we include quality checks in pilot scope.

Concrete next steps (agreeable to you):
1) We send a conservative TCO workbook (attached) plus a sample traffic template for you to confirm real qps/percent reuse. (Action: Tessa)
2) You share a prioritized list of 10 representative prompts we should target for prefix caching. (Action: Alicia)
3) Technical kickoff: 30–45 minute session next week to map integration touchpoints and canary sizing. (Action: schedule)

Attachments: [Attachment: stratuspay-tco-v1.xlsx (xlsx, 128KB)], [Attachment: sample-traffic.json (json, 35KB)], [Attachment: pilot-scope.pdf (pdf, 65KB)].

Thanks — I'll follow up with proposed times for the kickoff and a short primer on the batching/cache knobs we recommend.

Best,

Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@stratuspay.com>

Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: cost & capacity tradeoffs for StratusPay (pilot scope & next steps)

Tessa — thanks for the clear notes and the workbook. Quick responses inline: 

> Baseline: you run an ensemble... average token/interaction today ~1.6k tokens.
That aligns with our telemetry for July–Aug (we'll attach a fuller export by EOD).

On the pilot & TCO: two asks from our side before we commit to a timeline:
1) Can you tighten the ROI assumptions? The leadership team wants a worst-case, mid-case, and best-case line for cost reduction and time-to-payback (12/24/36 months).
2) We need to understand operational constraints — e.g., can we do a canary limited to a single region and single shard to start? We cannot risk global rollout until we validate quality.

Also, on caching: our prompt variability is medium-high for support flows, low for authorization microprompts (so caching should help some flows much more than others).

I'll upload the telemetry (anonymized) and our top-10 prompts by EOD. In the meantime can you confirm an initial pilot size (qps and throughput) you think is reasonable for canary?

Appreciate it — Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Platform Engineering | StratusPay
alicia.gomez@stratuspay.com

Alicia — appreciate the fast turnaround. Attached is an updated workbook with conservative, mid, and optimistic lines for spend reduction and payback (see tab: "sensitivity-summary"). We kept the quality checks baked into the pilot plan (quantization A/B only on non-critical flows at first).

Proposed canary sizing (conservative):
- Region: us-west-2 only; single shard, 3x A10g-equivalent GPUs (can scale to 5 if hit-rate is higher).
- Target: up to 600 qps steady, p95 < 300ms on critical flows with batching window at 50ms and prefix cache for top 50 prompts.
- Success criteria: 40%+ unit-cost reduction in mid-case OR no degradation in critical-flow quality.

Next steps:
- Alicia: upload telemetry + top-10 prompts (you mentioned EOD, thanks).
